rights.heading: No Surprises Act/Good Faith Estimate
rights.lead: You have the right to receive a “Good Faith Estimate” explaining how much your medical and mental health care will cost.

lawParagraphs.text: Under Section 2799B-6 of the Public Health Service Act, health care providers and health care facilities are required to inform individuals who are not enrolled in a plan or coverage or a Federal health care program, or not seeking to file a claim with their plan or coverage both orally and in writing of their ability, upon request or at the time of scheduling health care items and services, to receive a “Good Faith Estimate” of expected charges.

Under the law, health care providers need to give clients who don’t have insurance or who are not using insurance an estimate of the expected charges for medical services, including psychotherapy services.

items.text: You have the right to receive a Good Faith Estimate for the total expected cost of any non-emergency items or services.
You can ask your health care provider, and any other provider you choose, for a Good Faith Estimate before you schedule a service.
If you receive a bill that is at least $400 more than your Good Faith Estimate, you can dispute the bill.
Make sure to save a copy or picture of your Good Faith Estimate.

paragraphs.text: Laurie L. Arena, MSW, PMHNP is the founder of The Sage Institute. She has been a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner since 2010. She earned her Master’s of Nursing degree from Boston College and then went on to complete a Psychopharmacology Fellowship through Cambridge Health Alliance in 2011. Prior to this, she obtained a Master of Social Work (MSW) from Boston University in 2006 with a concentration in Group Work. Her training as a social worker paved a foundation of therapy skills and was also rooted in the social work tradition of advocating for human rights. Her undergraduate degree is from Queens University of Charlotte as a double major in Music and Psychology. Laurie has also completed a 200-hour level Yoga Teacher Training through Seaside Yoga in Wilmington, NC in 2009.

Laurie has worked in various mental health settings including Inpatient Psychiatric Units, Outpatient Treatment, Detox/Substance Abuse Treatment, Addiction Services, Crisis Stabilization Unit, Psychiatric Emergency Room, Assisted Living Facilities, Middle and High School school-based therapy program, and with an ACT (Assertive Community Treatment) Team, which entails working with clients with severe and persistent mental illness (primarily psychotic disorders) in the community and utilizes an interdisciplinary, person-centered, and empowerment model. In addition to her work with The Sage Institute, Laurie is also currently pursuing a PhD in Nursing at Case Western Reserve University, with a focus on nutrition and mental health-related research.

Personally, Laurie is anchored by her family, yoga, meditation, a vegan diet, nature, and music. She has learned through her travels to appreciate the importance of connecting to each moment, grounded by the ebb and flow of each breath, and to stay connected to one’s heart, emotions, values, and body while facing and interacting with the world. She believes there is intrinsic value and healing potential in all human beings and that science, medical advances, art, therapy, spirituality, and healing traditions can all combine to offer a reprieve from suffering and to support us in living our most meaningful, vibrant, and empowered life.

philosophy.heading: Laurie’s Philosophy
philosophy.intro: My approach to supporting people with their mental health needs is holistic and comprehensive. I specialize in Psychopharmacology and Lifestyle or Holistic Psychiatry. I also offer Mindfulness and Meditation techniques, Yoga for Mental Health, Psychoeducation, Nutritional Psychiatry, and Psychotherapy — with a focus on coping skills, self-compassion, and assertive communication and boundaries. My work is trauma-informed, LGBTQIA-allied, and prioritizes inclusion and social justice.

medication.heading: A thoughtful approach to medication
medication.body: My philosophy with psychiatric medications is to work with you to find the most effective medications, with the fewest risks or adverse effects. While for some people numerous psychiatric medications may be necessary, with distinct mechanisms of action, I work to avoid or reduce polypharmacy.
medication.disclaimer: As a disclaimer, I prescribe controlled substances sparingly and only for FDA-approved indications. Many supplements and herbal remedies have an evidence base for psychiatric conditions, and while I can discuss such research and options with you, I do not formally prescribe supplements (although most do not require a prescription).

bio.text: Jade Montana, PMHNP, CNM, FNP is a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner and a practicing Certified Nurse Midwife with additional Family Nurse Practitioner training.

Jade provides psychiatric medication management services integrated with supportive therapy. She practices with patience and open-mindedness to help meet you where you are. Visits are tailored toward your needs and goals. Jade can help you decide if psychiatric medication is right for you and work with you to optimize your medication plan, as well as consider a range of interventions to support your mental health. Jade’s goal is to ensure you have a safe place — without stigma or judgement — to be yourself, and to grow.

quotes.text: The mind, body, and soul are at the core of each individual. We are all unique and should be treated as such.

Mental health is like the tide of the ocean — as the tide comes in and the waves crash against the sand, it can be difficult to find the seashells. This is comparable to what we can experience during times of anxiety, turmoil, stress, and change. It is my job to help you calm the sea, cultivate peace of mind, and find your shell.
I believe safety is first, then discovery, and eventually moving on to recovery. Taking a holistic approach and prioritizing your mental health is imperative for your wellbeing.

bio.text: I believe that no one should be made to feel guilty about their struggles with mental health, and that everyone deserves to have a safe place to talk about these issues. Just as every person is unique, there is no one right way to treat mental illness. I strive to approach each individual with this in mind, knowing that they may have been through many treatment options already.

I know this can be a challenging and frustrating process, but I will listen to your concerns and work with you through the journey. My primary focus is on medication management, while also incorporating lifestyle modifications because of the connection between physical and mental health. My experience includes working with adolescents and adults with a variety of mental health concerns, including depression and anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders, and substance use disorders.

bio.text: Life can feel overwhelming at times, and when you’re struggling, it’s easy to feel like you’re carrying the weight of everything on your own. Whether you’re facing anxiety, depression, trauma, burnout, relationship challenges, or a major life transition, you deserve support from someone who will walk alongside you.

As a psychiatric provider and nurse with 13 years of experience in emergency medicine and the operating room, I have cared for people during some of their most vulnerable moments. Those experiences taught me the value of compassion, connection, and truly listening to each person’s story. When you work with me, you’ll find someone who combines years of nursing experience with a trauma-informed, compassionate approach to mental health care — because I understand that healing isn’t linear.

bio.text: Integrative Health Coach and Certified Personal Trainer

Wellness is about more than exercise, nutrition, or moving through life in a state of zen-like serenity. It is about developing a healthier and more compassionate relationship with your body and thoughts while finding practical ways to care for yourself within the realities of your life.
My own path to wellness has included physical injuries, mental health challenges, substance use challenges, and the ongoing cultivation of self-acceptance and self-compassion. These experiences shaped my belief that meaningful change does not require perfection. It begins with meeting yourself where you are, identifying what matters to you, and taking manageable steps guided by your values.
As an integrative health coach and certified personal trainer, I help clients incorporate strength training, cardiovascular exercise, mindfulness, movement, and practical nutrition into their daily lives. My approach is supportive, collaborative, and tailored to each person’s abilities, needs, and goals. Whether you are returning to movement, navigating physical or emotional limitations, building confidence, or simply trying to feel stronger and more in tune with your body and mind, we will develop an approach that works for you.
I am also pursuing a Master of Social Work to deepen my understanding of the relationship between physical health and emotional well-being. My particular interests include mobility across the lifespan, psychological flexibility, and creating sustainable change without shame or rigid expectations.

I believe mental health and movement are deeply connected. Strength and cardiovascular training can support mobility, confidence, independence, and quality of life at every age. Mindfulness and meditation can help cultivate psychological flexibility and emotional resilience. Any effective program, however, must be adapted to the individual.
Together, we may use progressive strength training to build physical capacity, cardiovascular exercise to support endurance and overall health, mindfulness and yoga principles to strengthen physical and emotional awareness, and practical nutrition strategies to support energy and well-being. Previous injuries, chronic conditions, or current limitations do not have to exclude you from meaningful movement or a compassionate relationship with yourself. Exercises can be adapted to respect your body’s present capacity while helping you safely work toward greater strength and mobility. Mindfulness and meditation can also be developed gradually through a variety of techniques. The raft that carries you across the river does not have to follow a predetermined design. It simply has to float.
My approach does not center on restrictive dieting, punishment, or “earning” food through exercise. We are not trying to tame the mind or crush uncomfortable feelings. Instead, I help clients develop realistic routines that nourish the body and mind, support everyday life, and remain flexible enough to be sustained over time.
Above all, coaching is a partnership. You are the expert on your life. My role is to offer knowledge, structure, encouragement, and practical tools while respecting your choices, boundaries, and goals.

Outside of coaching and graduate study, I am the proud father of four young daughters who keep me active, curious, and grounded. I also enjoy coding and web development, which reflect the same problem-solving mindset I bring to coaching: understanding how different pieces work together and finding solutions that fit the individual rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all formula.

I am currently a Master of Social Work candidate and hold a Bachelor of Arts in Music. My certifications through the American Council on Exercise include Certified Personal Trainer, Health Coach, Nutrition Specialist, and Group Fitness Instructor. I am also a 200-hour Registered Yoga Teacher and mindfulness meditation practitioner, with more than three years of experience helping clients build strength, improve well-being, and develop routines they can carry into everyday life.

posts.title: Book Recommendation: Good Inside by Dr. Becky Kennedy
posts.author: Laurie Arena
posts.excerpt: Book Recommendation and Summary: "Good Inside" by Dr. Becky Kennedy
posts.body:
Parenting is the hardest and most rewarding thing I've done in my life. And although there might not be a "one-size-fits-all" manual for the best way to raise each particular child, this book comes as close to that as you can get. Even as someone trained in mental health and therapy modalities, prior to reading this book, I had not been exposed to these concepts applied to parenting. 

I used to think in more reward and consequence terms. If my child engaged in "bad" behaviors such as yelling, hitting, throwing, name-calling, or the quintessential, "no" when they were told to do something, I thought it was my job to implement an immediate consequence and "not permit" or "stop" the behavior. Until I realized that the disconnection of the consequence and the stalemate of a power struggle were not only not working to curb the behaviors, but at a deeper level, they were backfiring. Disconnection, harshness, and strict punishments or consequences often lead to shame.  Internalized shame fuels further disconnection, destructive behaviors, and other mental health concerns. 

"CONNECTION FIRST," a core tenet of the book, has revolutionized my parenting and my own healing process. Now I have been given permission to tune into my child first, describe their behavior and inquire about and validate their emotions, STILL SET THE BOUNDARY, remind them they are a good kid and I love them, and more often than not, once they've settled down, the interactions end in a hug. Children need to feel safe and connected to learn. In reflecting on their behavior with them, once regulation has been restored, and couching the conversation in messages of their inherent goodness (GOOD INSIDE), my children receive the gift of the space to see how emotions and dysregulation drive their own behavior without being shamed. These are hard skills for adults to learn (regulation, examining our own behavior without self-shaming or inflated defensiveness, loving accountability).   

Any parent, expecting parent, grandparent, family member, caretaker, teacher, coach, counselor, or anyone who has children in their life, as well as every other human who wants to reflect on their own childhood and human relationships and psychology in general, can benefit from reading (or listening to, like I do!) to this book. Thank you, Dr. Becky, for the gift this book!!! So many adults and children will have better connection, healing, and improved mental health because of your encouragement.
